top_choice_rationale: P002 (B038: Autor, Hanson, Katz) recognises one mature body of empirical work on a single question, how technology and trade shift labour demand and who bears the adjustment. The core work spans roughly the early 1990s to the 2010s, with transparent designs that have been replicated, contested and refined in the open. Each name anchors a documented strand: Katz the long-run wage-structure and education-versus-technology benchmark, Autor the task and trade-shock evidence, and Hanson regional adjustment. I would word the citation around the empirical findings, namely the direction, concentration and persistence of adjustment. It should not claim the whole task framework, which leaves room for Acemoglu, Levy and Murnane, and it should not claim a final verdict on China-shock magnitudes. The main costs are real. The three-name cap excludes Dorn, the strands could be read as two discoveries, and shift-share identification and persistence remain debated. I still rank it above P001 (B044: Melitz, Helpman) because its evidence base is broader and more tested. P001 has a cleaner originating model, but it leaves out Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, and its welfare magnitudes depend on functional-form assumptions. I would find P001 an acceptable award if P002 cannot assemble a majority. I rank both above no award because each has substantial achievement, maturity and a defensible credit boundary. This ranking rests on those criteria and not on the round-2 support counts.
recusal_note: None apparent from profile. My supplied profile documents no co-authorship or institutional tie to Autor, Hanson, Katz, Dorn, Melitz or Helpman. Disclosed connections are my SSE affiliation with committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, my Lund colleagues including Enflo, and my co-authors in matching, auctions and market design, none of whom is a credited name on P001 or P002. Disclosed, not adjudicated.
